2027-02-06.title: Fifth Saturday of Denha
2027-02-06.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: I am standing at the door, knocking
2027-02-06.alt: Season of Denha. Last day of the Season of Denha. Tomorrow is the First Sunday of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba); the fast itself begins on Monday.
2027-02-06.verse: Listen! I am standing at the door, knocking; if you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in to you and eat with you, and you with me.
theo: The last of the seven letters in Revelation is written to Laodicea, a rich banking city, proud of its textiles and its famous eye-salve, whose water came by aqueduct and arrived lukewarm. The risen Christ, “the Amen, the faithful and true witness”, speaks to it bluntly: “I know your works; you are neither cold nor hot. I wish that you were either cold or hot. So, because you are lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I am about to spit you out of my mouth.” Their real sickness is self-satisfaction: “For you say, ‘I am rich, I have prospered, and I need nothing.’ You do not realize that you are wretched, pitiable, poor, blind, and naked.” So he offers them what they think they already have: gold refined by fire, white robes, salve for their eyes. His harshness is love: “I reprove and discipline those whom I love. Be earnest, therefore, and repent.” And then the gentlest words in the whole book: “Listen! I am standing at the door, knocking; if you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in to you and eat with you, and you with me.” The Lord does not break the door down. He knocks, and he waits.

The last Gospel of Denha is a picture of the opposite of Laodicea. Jesus goes up a mountain by the Sea of Galilee and sits down. Great crowds come, “bringing with them the lame, the maimed, the blind, the mute, and many others. They put them at his feet, and he cured them.” These people do not say, I need nothing. They lay their poverty at his feet, and the crowd is amazed “when they saw the mute speaking, the maimed whole, the lame walking, and the blind seeing. And they praised the God of Israel.” Through these weeks of Denha Christ has been revealed: at the Jordan, at Cana, to the first disciples, to Nicodemus, to the Samaritans, to the sick. Tomorrow the Great Fast begins. It is not a season for the self-satisfied, but for those who admit that they are poor and blind, open the door to the one who knocks, and let themselves be carried to his feet.
outline: Ask: is your faith hot, cold, or lukewarm?
The danger of saying: I need nothing.
Point 3 · I stand at the door
He knocks and waits; he wants to eat with us.
The crowd that brought its poverty to Jesus.
“I am standing at the door, knocking.”
live: Before the Great Fast begins, make a good confession or plan when you will make it.
Pray today for one sick or disabled person by name, and visit or call them if you can.
2027-02-06.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, faithful and true witness, you stand at the door of our hearts and knock. Forgive our lukewarmness and our pride that says we need nothing. Clothe us in white, anoint our eyes to see, and as the Great Fast begins, let us lay all our poverty at your feet and open the door to you, so that you may come in and eat with us. Amen.
altar: At every Holy Qurbana the promise of Revelation is fulfilled: the Lord comes in and eats with us, and we with him.

quick: The Laodiceans were lukewarm and said: we need nothing.
Christ stands at the door and knocks; if we open, he will come in and eat with us.
The crowds laid their sick at Jesus' feet, and he cured them.
2027-02-06.action: Make or plan a good confession before the Great Fast begins.
2027-02-06.question: Is there any area where I say to God: I need nothing?

family.explain: Jesus says: I am standing at your door, knocking. If you open, I will come in and eat with you! Many people brought sick friends to Jesus, and he healed them all.
family.intention: We pray for the sick, and for a good beginning of the Great Fast.
family.ask: Ask: “What will our family do for Jesus in this Great Fast?”

illus: A young professional in Kochi, successful and busy, went to the Holy Qurbana only at Christmas and Easter. When a friend asked if he prayed, he laughed: I have everything I need. A few months later his company closed and his father fell ill in the same week. Sitting late at night in the hospital corridor, he found himself reading the words on a picture on the wall: I am standing at the door, knocking. He said later: I had kept the door locked because I thought I was rich. That night I opened it.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you stand at the door and knock. We open the door to you; come in and stay with us. Amen.
share: Because you are lukewarm, I am about to spit you out of my mouth (Revelation 3:16). Where am I lukewarm?
If you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in (Revelation 3:20). What keeps my door closed?
They put them at his feet, and he cured them (Matthew 15:30). Whom will I bring to Jesus' feet?
pm.resp: Lord, come in and stay with us.
interc: For the whole Church, that the Great Fast may be a time of true conversion.
For those who are lukewarm or have drifted away.
For the sick and the disabled.
For those who think they need nothing.
For our group, that we may open the door to Christ.
pm.close: Father, your Son knocks at our door and heals all who are laid at his feet. Prepare us for the Great Fast with humble and open hearts. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the risen Christ writes to the church of Laodicea: I know your works; you are neither cold nor hot (Revelation 3:15). They were rich and said: we need nothing. But they did not see that they were poor, blind and naked.

His words are hard, but they come from love: I reprove and discipline those whom I love. And then: listen! I am standing at the door, knocking; if you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in to you and eat with you (Revelation 3:20).
In the Gospel great crowds bring the lame, the maimed, the blind and the mute and put them at Jesus' feet, and he cures them all. They did not pretend to be rich. They brought their poverty to him.
Tomorrow the Great Fast begins. Let us not be lukewarm. Let us admit our need, open the door with a good confession, and lay ourselves at his feet. Then he will come in and eat with us. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: I am knocking at your door! When we pray and say sorry for our sins, we open the door, and Jesus comes in to be our friend. Will you open the door for Jesus?

intro: Theme: “I am standing at the door, knocking.”
The lukewarm church, the Lord who knocks, and the crowds who laid their poverty at his feet.

q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
I know your works; you are neither cold nor hot. I wish that you were either cold or hot.
points.apply: Name one area where you have grown lukewarm, and choose one act of fervour for the Great Fast.

sub: He does not break the door.
He wants to eat with us.
q: I slept, but my heart was awake. Listen! my beloved is knocking. “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my perfect one;
Listen! I am standing at the door, knocking; if you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in to you and eat with you, and you with me.
points.apply: Open the door with a good confession before or early in the Great Fast.

sub: The lame, the blind, the mute.
They praised the God of Israel.
q: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped; then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the speechless sing for joy.
Great crowds came to him, bringing with them the lame, the maimed, the blind, the mute, and many others. They put them at his feet, and he cured them,
points.apply: Bring a sick or disabled person to Jesus in prayer, and visit them this week.

concl: Christ knocks at the door of every lukewarm heart.
Admit your poverty, open the door, and let him carry you into the Great Fast.
2027-02-06.resolve: Begin the Great Fast with a good confession and one concrete act of fervour.
